newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks pare losses on pre-weekend buying.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks pare losses on pre-weekend buying.

text.p: Mexican stocks cut earlier losses at the close Friday on pre-weekend buying, but still ended lower amid a drop on Wall Street.
"Stocks bottomed out at the 3,660-point mark, which is where some local buyers stepped in. A rebound in the Dow (Jones industrial average) also helped," said a trader at the Bancomer brokerage.
The leading IPC share index ended down 14.62 points, or 0.40 percent, at 3,680.56, but off a session low of 3,663.25.
The Dow meanwhile closed down 0.88 percent, or 59.27 points, at 6,696.48 after falling as low as 6,662.23.
Analysts said share prices fell due to a continued bout of profit-taking, as well as the adverse effect of declines on Wall Street.
"It's the correction we had been expecting for days. It's very normal and healthy profit-taking," said Jaime Fernandez, an equity analyst at the Interacciones brokerage.
On the broad market, a total of 106 stocks changed hands, of which 55 declined while 29 finished ahead amid moderate trading volume of 76.3 million shares.
Retail stock Cifra A series headed the sliders' list, off 1.30 pesos (17 cents) at 9.60 pesos ($1.23).
"Cifra A shares were traded at little volume. They're less liquid than other series and can be easily manipulated by small up- and downticks and small trades," a trader said.
Cifra was followed by holding company Accelsa, off 9 centavos (1 cent) at 1.66 pesos (13 cents).
"I would say Accelsa fell because it is infrequently traded and dealers finally decided to take profits on it," a dealer said.
Retail stock Ceramic ULD series gained 2.02 pesos (26 cents) to 12.00 ($1.54) to head the gainers' list, on what traders said was a favourable 1996 earnings report posted last week.
Dealers saw a rough ride for the bourse in the week ahead, with important U.S. economic data in the offing, such as advance fourth qaurter gross domestic product and existing home sales.
"We still see the market sliding, on Monday at least, but we sould recover once the coast is clearer for U.S. financial markets," a broker said.
